record.paper_title: Monetary Stabilization in Cryptocurrencies—Design Approaches and Open Questions
record.original_question: Can an effectively price-stable cryptocurrency be realized in a fully permissionless setting, where the system cannot assume that participants are identifiable or trustworthy?

evidence.quote:
Departing from mainly economic questions, we will now
discuss the design of stable cryptocurrencies in terms of their
”decentralization” and ”trustlessness”—notions that cryptocur-
rencies are commonly associated with and potentially owe
their popularity to. We focus on contrasting fully permis-
sionless systems, i.e., systems that function without previous
assumptions about the identiﬁability of participants or their
trustworthiness, with architectures in which the existence of
a group of well-known trusted actors must be assumed. With
the current state of knowledge, it is an outstanding question
whether an effectively price-stable cryptocurrency can at all
be realized in a fully permissionless setting.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed cryptocurrency protocol operating in a fully permissionless setting, defined as a system in which no prior assumptions can be made about the identifiability, reputation, or trustworthiness of participants: any party may join or leave the protocol at any time under arbitrary (possibly Sybil) identities, and there is no designated set of trusted actors. Call such a cryptocurrency "effectively price-stable" if its protocol guarantees, with high probability and against a rational/adversarial subset of participants, that the exchange rate of one unit of the cryptocurrency, measured against some specified external reference asset (e.g., a fiat currency or a basket of goods), remains within a bounded neighborhood of a target value over arbitrarily long time horizons, despite fluctuations in demand and adversarial behavior.

Question: Does there exist a protocol for a cryptocurrency that is simultaneously (i) fully permissionless in the above sense and (ii) effectively price-stable in the above sense? Equivalently, prove either the existence of such a protocol (by construction together with a security/stability analysis) or an impossibility theorem showing that no such protocol can exist under standard cryptographic and economic assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: No published result is known that either constructs a provably price-stable cryptocurrency in a fully permissionless setting or proves a formal impossibility. Existing decentralized stablecoins (e.g., DAI, RAI, algorithmic designs) rely on collateral, oracles, or governance assumptions, and several have failed (e.g., Terra/UST in 2022). The question therefore appears to remain open.
